chunks: “Sadir entered upon my father عليه السلام during the month of Ramadan. He said to him: ‘O Sadir, do you know what nights these are?’ He said to him: ‘Yes, may I be your ransom, these are the nights of the month of Ramadan, so what is it?’ My father said to him: ‘Are you able to free, on every night of these nights, ten slaves from the descendants of Ismaʿil?’ Sadir said to him: ‘May my father and mother be for you, my wealth does not reach that.’ So he kept reducing it until he brought it down to one slave, while in all of that he was saying: ‘I am not able to do it.’ Then he said to him: ‘Then are you able to provide iftar each night to one Muslim man?’ He said to him: ‘Yes, and ten as well.’ My father عليه السلام said to him: ‘That is what I intended, O Sadir. Indeed, your providing iftar to your Muslim brother is equal to the freeing of one slave from the descendants of Ismaʿil عليه السلام.’”

key_terms.اللَّيَالِي: the nights being referred to as especially blessed nights in Ramadan
key_terms.تُفَطِّرَ: to provide iftar, meaning to give food for breaking the fast
key_terms.رِقَابٍ: slaves whose emancipation is described as a great virtuous act
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the sacred month of fasting
key_terms.عِتْقَ: the emancipation or freeing of a slave
key_terms.مُسْلِمًا: a Muslim person who is the recipient of the iftar
key_terms.يَعْدِلُ: is equal in reward or equivalent in merit

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for providing iftar to a fasting Muslim in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the great reward of providing iftar in the month of Ramadan. Imam Jaʿfar al-Sadiq عليه السلام relates that feeding a Muslim at iftar carries a reward comparable to freeing a slave, showing the immense spiritual value of generosity and care for fellow believers.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1953 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Sadir entered upon my father (as) during the Month of Ramadan.
My father said to him: 'O Sadir, do you know what nights these are?'
Sadir replied: 'Yes, may I be your ransom; these are the nights of the Month of Ramadan. Why do you ask?'
My father (as) said to him: 'Can you free ten slaves from the descendants of Isma'il every night of these nights?'
Sadir replied: 'May I be your ransom, my wealth cannot reach that amount.'
My father (as) continued to reduce the number until he said: 'Can you free one slave every night?' Sadir replied: 'I cannot do that either.'
My father (as) then asked: 'Can you provide iftar for one Muslim every night?'
Sadir replied: 'Yes, I can, and even for ten Muslims.'
My father (as) said: 'That is what I intended, O Sadir. Providing iftar to your Muslim brother is equal to freeing one slave from the descendants of Isma'il (as).'"
